meta.source: Hand-scored against the frequency analysis in topics.json, question by question.
meta.note: A paper is scored once it has been sat. Marks are the paper's own; the verdict says whether the checklist already carried the topic the question asks for. Every total on the page is summed from these questions — nothing is stored twice.

verdicts.on: The checklist already carried this topic.
verdicts.partly: The chapter is on the list, but not the angle this question takes.
verdicts.off: Nothing on the checklist points at this.

scored.name: Paper 020601 (set A)
scored.label: Pathology & Microbiology
scored.choice: Question 4 prints five parts for 5×4=20, so four of the five get written.
scored.caveat: Scored on a photograph of page 2 only. The paper's year and session are not printed on that page, and any further section — the other 020601 papers carry a Part C of MCQs — is not in the photograph.

questions.text: Define oedema. Write down its pathogenesis. Write in detail about renal oedema.
questions.note: Five transcribed papers ask the first two thirds word for word. The renal third is new — the topic is scoped to pulmonary and cardiac.
One MCQ mention on record — “oncogenic viruses in humans”, 2021. No written question, ever. The nearest topic, Carcinogenesis (Chemical, Radiation), is a different answer.
A total blind spot: zero mentions in the checklist and zero across all 104 transcribed papers. Nothing on the list points at premalignant oral lesions.
This paper code opened with it in 2022 — “Define WHO criteria for diagnosis of diabetes mellitus.”

questions.text: Give a brief note on types and pathogenesis of tuberculosis. Describe their laboratory diagnosis and prevention.
questions.note: Joint-heaviest topic in the subject, and asked in eight transcribed papers besides.

questions.text: Give a short note on moist heat sterilization.
questions.note: The other joint-heaviest, and asked in almost these words nine times in the transcribed set alone.

questions.text: What is mycosis? Describe types of Mycoses.
questions.note: The Mycology chapter is four named organisms — Candidiasis, Cryptococcus, oral lesions in systemic mycoses, dermatophytes. There is no “define and classify mycoses” entry, and the same framing went unmapped once before, in 2011.
The cheapest five marks on the paper, and exactly the topic a frequency ranking tells you to leave until last.

questions.text: Differentiate between acquired and innate immunity.
questions.note: Asked as printed in 2012, 2013, 2016 and again on this paper code in 2023.

questions.text: Describe any two commonly known protozoan disease.
questions.note: The two heaviest topics in Parasitology are, between them, the whole answer.

gaps.name: Leukoplakia
gaps.note: Zero mentions in the checklist and zero across all 104 transcribed papers. Nothing on the list points at premalignant oral lesions. Worth its own topic under Neoplasia.

gaps.name: Oncogenes
gaps.note: One MCQ mention on record, no written question ever. Either a new topic for the molecular basis of cancer, or widen Carcinogenesis to name them.

gaps.name: Renal oedema
gaps.note: Part of question 1. The topic exists but is scoped to pulmonary and cardiac — widen it to Pulmonary/Cardiac/Renal.

gaps.name: Classification of mycoses
gaps.note: The Mycology chapter names four organisms and never asks you to define or classify the group. Skippable here, but cheap to add.

scored.name: Paper 020501
scored.label: Pharmacology
scored.choice: Questions 2 and 4 each print five short notes for 4×5=20, so four of the five get written.
scored.caveat: Scored on photographs of pages 2 and 3. Part C — ten one-mark MCQs — is left out of the scoring entirely rather than judged on a fifth of itself: only two of its ten items were photographed. Both of those two were answerable off the checklist (adrenaline with a local anaesthetic, and penicillin as a bactericidal). The cover page carrying the sitting and date was not photographed either.

questions.text: Classify drugs used in the treatment of diabetes mellitus. Describe in detail role of traditional and newer insulins in management of diabetes.
questions.note: Called exactly. A HIGH topic at 10× that has opened three other transcribed papers with almost this stem — 6334, 7223 and 7190 all say classify the antidiabetics. The one new turn is "newer insulins": the analogues have never been asked before, and the topic's own name leans on the oral drugs, metformin and the sulfonylureas.

The one real miss, and not a new one. Propranolol has now been asked seven times across the transcribed papers — including two full 10-mark openers, "classify beta blockers", in 7808 and 6499 — and there is still no topic to tick, because the source analysis lists an Autonomic Nervous System chapter and puts no table under it.
HIGH at 7×, and asked as a short note in four other papers on file. Free marks.
The topic names LMWH outright. The December 2023 paper under this same code asked for it in the same words, one sitting ago.

A genuine first: no transcribed paper has ever printed the word serotonin, and the CNS chapter carries no antidepressant topic at all. Less a failure of the checklist than a new arrival — and with four of five to write, the one to leave.

questions.text: Transdermal Therapeutic Systems for Drug Delivery.
questions.note: The chapter is there but the angle is not. Routes of Administration is the lightest topic in General Pharmacology at 3×, and it is scoped to the parenteral routes — transdermal has never been asked before, in any paper on file.

questions.text: Classify diuretic drugs. Describe uses and adverse effects of thiazide and loop diuretics.
questions.note: HIGH at 9×, and the topic names frusemide, thiazides and high-ceiling — all three halves of the question. Worth noting the promotion: every previous appearance was a 4-mark short note on high ceiling diuretics. This is the first time it has carried a 10-mark question.

Penicillins is the heaviest thing in Chemotherapy at 12× and the topic names amoxicillin. The clavulanic acid pairing is new wording, but it is one line of beta-lactamase inhibition on top of an answer the checklist already had.
Paper 7496 asked for "drugs for dental plaque" in almost these words.

No topic of its own. NSAIDs / Aspirin is HIGH at 10× and covers the ground around it, but paracetamol is not an NSAID and the topic is written around aspirin. It has come up bare once before, on 7172, plus the N-acetylcysteine poisoning angle. The weakest of these five, so the one to drop.
The single heaviest topic in the subject: 14× in the analysis, 15 questions across the transcribed papers. If anything was safe, it was this.
HIGH at 8×, asked outright in 5743 and 6499.

gaps.name: Beta blockers / Propranolol
gaps.note: The structural hole. The Autonomic Nervous System chapter exists in the analysis with no topics under it, yet propranolol and adrenaline between them account for fifteen questions across the transcribed papers, two of them 10-mark openers. Everything else here is a wording gap; this one is a missing chapter.

gaps.name: Transdermal drug delivery
gaps.note: Routes of Administration is on the list but scoped to parenteral, and sits at LOW. Widening it to name the transdermal and oral routes would have covered this.

gaps.name: Paracetamol
gaps.note: Asked bare twice now and still has no topic. Either its own entry or a rename of NSAIDs / Aspirin to take in the non-NSAID analgesics.

gaps.name: SSRIs / antidepressants
gaps.note: Zero appearances in any paper on file before today, so there was nothing to predict it with. Worth adding now that it has been asked once.
